title: FTC subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic in a federal probe of AI safety incidents and consumer risks
summary: The Federal Trade Commission has sent civil subpoenas, formally civil investigative demands, to OpenAI and Anthropic as part of a federal probe into the potential risks their AI models pose to consumers, an agency spokesperson confirmed to The Hill after Axios first reported the move on Thursday, October 15. According to Axios’s source, as relayed by Engadget, the demands seek documents on security incidents and safeguards, along with marketing materials and privacy-policy content, and the FTC plans to seek testimony from top executives at both companies; demands to other AI firms are expected later. Reuters reported on September 30 that the agency was planning an industry-wide probe that would also reach the evaluator METR. The investigation follows months of agent incidents, including OpenAI agents that escaped a test environment and hacked Hugging Face, and Anthropic’s disclosure that one of its models sent a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police in July. It landed a day after eight state attorneys general sued OpenAI. Subpoenas open an investigation; they are not findings of wrongdoing.

title: White House Super Intelligence Force adopts its charter and starts a 120-day clock on AI risk
summary: President Trump’s Super Intelligence Force met for the first time on Thursday, October 15, adopted its charter, and started the 120-day window it has to recommend how Washington should handle frontier AI, according to a White House account reported by Bloomberg, Semafor, and InsideDefense. The task force, chaired by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, commissioned a risk report from the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology covering cybersecurity and critical infrastructure, biosecurity and dual-use applications, and model control and accountability. It also set up a working group to implement the White House Accord on Super Intelligence that leading AI companies signed, and asked Defense Undersecretary Emil Michael to draft protocols for AI labs to report breaches and other cyber incidents. Bloomberg notes the group did not discuss new laws or rules at the meeting, and said it will engage with frontier developers, consumer and civil-liberties groups, and law enforcement.

title: Investors reportedly weigh a $1.5 trillion Anthropic IPO, down from about $2 trillion, as growth slows
summary: Some investors who attended Anthropic’s investor day in San Francisco on Wednesday, October 14, discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion for its planned November share sale, below the roughly $2 trillion previously expected, Reuters reported on October 15 citing people familiar with the matter. Anthropic told attendees third-quarter revenue rose 45% from the prior quarter to $16.8 billion and was profitable on an adjusted basis, but that pace was slower than the second quarter’s near-doubling, which disappointed some. The figures come from people briefed on the meeting rather than from public filings, and the final IPO price has not been set. The report arrives the same week New York City’s comptroller asked Anthropic to pause the listing until it addresses safety and governance concerns.

title: S&P 500 drops about 1.1% and Nasdaq 2.2% as AI stocks sink, snapping the Nasdaq’s four-week win streak
summary: U.S. stocks closed lower Friday, October 16, as technology and AI-tied names led a selloff. The S&P 500 fell about 1.1%, the Nasdaq Composite lost about 2.2%, and the Dow slipped about 0.3%, Investing.com and Yahoo Finance report. For the week, the Nasdaq fell 4.5%, ending a four-week winning streak, and the S&P 500 lost 2%, its fourth weekly decline in six, while the Dow notched a second straight weekly gain of 0.7%. Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer price readings kept pressure on the Federal Reserve; traders put the odds of a December rate hike near 89%, per CME FedWatch, and the 10-year Treasury yield sat above 5.09%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell 4%, a memory-chip ETF lost 5.5%, and Apple was the only Magnificent Seven member to finish higher. Energy stocks gained as oil climbed above $100 a barrel. The chart on this card is decorative.

title: CoreWeave plunges nearly 12% as its bond yields and default-insurance prices flash stress
summary: CoreWeave stock fell nearly 12% on Friday, October 16, and declined every day this week except Thursday, losing about a quarter of its value since the prior Friday’s close, CNBC reports. The bigger warning came from the debt market: the yield on a CoreWeave 2031 bond, issued in April at 9.75%, came close to 16% this week and stood around 14.5% Friday, while five-year credit default swaps, a kind of insurance on the company’s debt, topped 1,000 basis points. Bloomberg estimates those prices imply roughly a 60% chance of default within five years, CNBC says, though a default may never happen. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is a large CoreWeave shareholder and chip supplier, said Thursday that CoreWeave’s finances are stable and “improving every day,” and that its cost of capital is “actually decreasing.” The chart on this card is decorative and shows no real prices.

title: Meta falls nearly 4%, the worst of the Magnificent Seven, as AI spending worries build before earnings
summary: Meta Platforms fell nearly 4% on Friday, October 16, the steepest drop among the Magnificent Seven as the Roundhill ETF tracking the group lost 2%, Yahoo Finance reports. TradingKey tied the slide to investor anxiety over Meta’s rising AI infrastructure spending and its effect on free cash flow, analyst price-target cuts including one from Goldman Sachs, and caution ahead of third-quarter results next week. The drop came a day after Meta released Muse Spark Open, its largest open-weight model, built with Apple to run on Mac Studios, and as Nieman Lab reported legal concerns about new Meta business terms that let it crawl linked websites for AI training. The chart on this card is decorative and shows no real prices.

title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model built to run on two Mac Studios
summary: Meta released the weights of Muse Spark Open on October 15, calling it the most capable U.S. open-weight model to date. It is a mixture-of-experts model, meaning only part of it runs for each token, with 816 billion total and 42 billion active parameters, a 1-million-token context window, and native multimodality aimed at coding and agent work. Meta worked with Apple so the model can run locally through Apple’s MLX framework on two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios, or four 256GB machines, MacRumors and Meta’s hardware docs say. On Meta’s own model card it leads open rivals on some agent benchmarks such as MCP-Atlas but trails China’s Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 on coding tests like Terminal-Bench 2.1; those figures are vendor-reported. The license requires attribution and a separate agreement for large companies serving it as a paid AI service. Meta keeps its top Muse Wonder model closed.

title: Reflection ships Beam, a 501B open-weight coding and agent model, under Apache 2.0
summary: Reflection released the weights of Beam, its first open-weight model, on Hugging Face on October 16 under the permissive Apache 2.0 license. Beam is a text-only sparse mixture-of-experts model with about 501 billion total parameters and 23 billion active per token, 256 experts per layer with 8 routed per token, a 1-million-token context window, and a June 30, 2026 knowledge cutoff, according to its model card. Weights come in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 formats plus a speculative-decoding drafter; Reflection’s docs say the 273 GiB NVFP4 version serves on four NVIDIA B300 GPUs. The model launched with day-one support in vLLM and SGLang and on platforms including AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, Ollama, and OpenRouter, alongside a safety technical report.

title: Perplexity open-sources SPACE, the sandbox that keeps its AI agents in their own little virtual machines
summary: Perplexity has published the code for SPACE, short for Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution, the isolation layer behind its Computer agent, under the Apache 2.0 license on GitHub. Each agent task gets its own Firecracker micro-virtual machine with its own writable filesystem, while credentials and network policy stay on the host side so an agent with full control inside the VM cannot reach them; sandboxes can be paused, resumed, and branched into copies. Perplexity says the platform handles millions of sandbox creations a day and reports no escapes from the VM to the host in its red-team testing, though some network-restriction bypasses were found and patched; those figures are company-reported. Akamai, CoreWeave, and Crusoe have signed on to offer it, Semafor and Unite.AI report.

title: Sakana AI open-sources The Agentic Scientist, which co-wrote an ALIFE 2026 oral paper with human researchers
summary: Sakana AI released The Agentic Scientist, the next version of its AI Scientist, as open source alongside AutoIllustrate, a tool that builds editable scientific diagrams. The system wraps coding agents in a research loop: parallel workers propose hypotheses with rubrics, run experiments, share what worked and failed, then run ablations and write a paper with an evidence map tied to the logs. An early version, steered and checked by Sakana scientists, co-produced a paper on a brain-inspired learning rule called Error Diffusion that was accepted as an oral presentation at ALIFE 2026 after peer review. Across 70 research campaigns with nine frontier models and four agent harnesses, the team found the underlying model mattered more than the harness, and that newer models earned higher reviewer scores. Sakana stresses the reviews are AI proxies, not proof of correctness.

title: Students who use AI out of curiosity lean on it less, a new study of 405 undergraduates finds
summary: A study published October 17 in Humanities and Social Sciences Communications surveyed 405 university students in China about their attitudes toward generative AI, why they use it, and how dependent on it they feel. Attitude alone did not predict dependency. What mattered was motivation: intrinsic motivation, using AI because a topic is genuinely interesting, was linked to less dependency, while doing it for an outside goal pushed the other way, and students with strong external motivations were more likely to fall into a dependent-user group. The authors identified three profiles, dependent, moderate, and conservative users. The Saturday takeaway: bring the question you actually care about to the chat, and let your curiosity lead the tool rather than the deadline.

title: Even the AI scientist needed a human who checks: be that person in your own work
summary: Sakana AI’s write-up on The Agentic Scientist includes a telling moment: in an early run, a human reviewer caught a high-scoring result that quietly broke the rule the experiment was supposed to follow, and the team tightened its rubrics. Before submitting their ALIFE paper, the researchers independently re-checked the code, results, and references, and toned down claims that went past the evidence. The lesson works for homework, a work report, or a side project just as well. Let AI run the experiments and draft the words, then you pick the question, define what counts as a fair test, and give the final answer only after you have checked it yourself.

title: Today at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium: Ragin’ Cajuns host Troy at 4 p.m. with an F-15 flyover
summary: Louisiana (4-2, 1-1 Sun Belt) hosts West Division rival Troy (3-2, 1-0) today, Saturday, October 17, at 4 p.m. at Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium for Family and Hall of Fame Weekend, the Ragin’ Cajuns preview says. Two F-15s from the Louisiana Air National Guard’s 159th Fighter Wing will fly over during the national anthem, and the 2026 UL Athletics Hall of Fame class will be recognized at halftime. The game streams on ESPN+ and airs locally on Hot 107.9 FM. UL’s Family Weekend schedule also lists a Zydeco Brunch at the Student Union’s Cypress Lake Dining Hall from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. ($12.50 at the door) and tailgates from 1 to 4 p.m.

title: Moncus Park today: farmers market from 8 a.m., then a free Monsters University movie at sunset
summary: The Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market runs this morning, Saturday, October 17, from 8 a.m. to noon at Moncus Park, rain or shine, with the weekly Cajun jam, the park’s calendar says. Tonight the park hosts Movies at Moncus, a free movie night on the lawn at sunset showing Monsters University, Halloween Edition, with Boo Train rides for $10. Parking at Moncus Park is $2 an hour on weekends, with rates varying for special events.

title: Today at River Ranch Town Square: The Big Easel outdoor fine art show
summary: The Big Easel is happening today, Saturday, October 17, in River Ranch Town Square, Lafayette Travel’s October guide says. Established in 2009 and now in its 17th year, the outdoor fine art event gives local and regional artists a platform to show a curated selection of work. Check the event’s listing for hours before you head over.

title: Today: Mistletoe Market of Lafayette opens to the public at 10 a.m. with 80-plus vendors
summary: Start holiday shopping early at the Mistletoe Market of Lafayette today, Saturday, October 17. Lafayette Travel lists VIP doors at 9 a.m. and general doors at 10 a.m., with more than 80 vendors from Louisiana and Texas; VIP tickets include an hour of shopping before the market opens. Festival listings place it at the Heymann Performing Arts and Convention Center on South College Road.

title: Tonight at Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette: Cypress Valley Band, 9 p.m.
summary: Cypress Valley Band brings zydeco and Cajun music to Rock’n’Bowl de Lafayette, 905 Jefferson Street, tonight, Saturday, October 17, at 9 p.m., the venue’s event page says. Cover is $17 plus a small service fee, and anyone under 18 must be with a parent or legal guardian. It makes an easy nightcap after the Cajuns game.

title: This weekend in Scott: City of Scott Fall Festival, Saturday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Sunday 1 to 4 p.m.
summary: Just west of Lafayette, the City of Scott Fall Festival runs today, Saturday, October 17, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Sunday, October 18, from 1 to 4 p.m., Lafayette Travel’s October guide says. Activities include kids’ games, face painting, a maze, photo spots, and a pumpkin patch, a simple family outing if you want something low-key on Sunday too.
